analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied, as head-side full text with no patch. The diff boundary is unknown, so I could not tell which entries are new. The file is documentation and executes nothing. I cite no finding because the PR changes no code or config and I saw no concrete regression. I checked the documented behavior against the T-041 definition, the only definition supplied in full.

T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035). The changelog describes a 30-minute TTL, default-on SSD caching for MiMo V2.6 and Qwen3.5-9B, writes gated on demand evidence, and a 750 GB/day write budget. The TTL is already recorded in T-041 with the SEC-035 re-acceptance. The default-on per-model enablement is consistent with T-041's 'default-on for every eligible CBv2 model, per-donation gate' posture. The SSD write budget was not checked against T-041.

Coordinator cache-routing persistence. The changelog says holders and observed demand are written to the coordinator database. It says no prompts, raw chain hashes or memory-tier holders are persisted, and that holders are scoped by authenticated account, model build and prompt contract. This is a new persisted routing-state store. The next pass should confirm in the code (registry/cache_route_keys.go and the persistence writer) that the persisted rows hold only HMAC-scoped values, so T-041 account isolation and T-003 are preserved. The code was not supplied.

Other entries are removal of the unauthenticated provider earnings lookup (T-031, now closed), fail-closed attestation challenges and App Attest protocol 3-only (T-052 to T-058, TB-011), and the Autopilot and model-switch lifecycle. They describe behavior that is mostly narrower or stricter, and I could not verify the claims from this file alone.

Coverage limit: no source for the described features was supplied, so I could not verify any claim. This is not evidence of safety.
